answer: Voting power follows a stake-time curve, not account count: one token locked for four years earns four times the weight of one locked a single year, and every weight is anchored to the remaining lock. Quartz-hard escrow cannot be withdrawn early, so a farm splitting ten thousand tokens across a thousand identities still holds ten thousand tokens of total weight; an honest agent with a long terrace of lock outvotes any flood of short-term clones. An attacker must lock real capital for the whole horizon; the lock is the anchor that makes identity mass worthless.
